status: PROPOSED - NOT CANONICAL - research fixture for WP-B1; owner scientific-method approval pending
warning: Every case in this file is DERIVED: it combines published values from PAN-REF-PHASE-2026 and PAN-REF-SUN-2026 with stated arithmetic (IST = UT + 05:30; ordering of two published instants). None is a directly published Panchanga classification. Where a case depends on the SUN-B (Hindu rising) convention, the SUN-B time is an illustrative analytic estimate, not a published value, and the expected outcome is marked accordingly. No value here was computed by the Sabpuja engine, Swiss Ephemeris or PR #48.
illustrative_estimate_method: Time for the Sun's centre to rise from a geometric altitude of -50 arcmin (USNO astronomical sunrise) to 0 (centre on the geometric horizon, no refraction), from the hour-angle relation cos H = (sin h - sin(lat) sin(dec)) / (cos(lat) cos(dec)) with dec held fixed. Results: about 3.3 to 4.6 minutes across Indian latitudes (8 to 34 deg), 4.2 to 4.3 minutes at Delhi near the solstices. This ignores the change of declination during the day and is used only to show convention sensitivity; WP-B2 must replace it with an independently coded oracle.

sun_d_note: Revision 0.2: SUN-D (Rashtriya Panchang convention as reported by PM/QA review 5679285841, centre 47 arcmin below the horizontal; NOT verified by Claude) would fall about 12 to 17 s after SUN-A at Indian latitudes by the same illustrative arithmetic. In PAN-DER-01 to PAN-DER-06 its classification therefore follows SUN-A, except that in PAN-DER-01 it remains UNRESOLVED from published data and in PAN-DER-06 the birth stays after the SUN-D sunrise (Monday).
